memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The rest of the people will hear of this and be afraid, and never again will such an evil thing be done among you. Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. - Deut 19:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God explains the purpose of just punishment, so that others would hear, take it seriously, and be restrained from doing evil. Then comes the well-known principle, "life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth." We often misunderstand this. Far from encouraging revenge, it was actually a limit on it. The punishment could not exceed the crime. It ensured that justice was proportionate, not driven by escalating rage.

In a world where people might repay an insult with murder, God's law said the response must match the offence, no more. This protected wrongdoers from excessive vengeance and restrained the cycle of retaliation. It placed justice in the hands of impartial judges rather than angry individuals.

Jesus later took this principle further for personal relationships. He taught His followers not to insist on retaliation at all, but to turn the other cheek and overcome evil with good (Matt 5:38-39). What the law restrained, grace transforms. The proper handling of justice belongs to God and to those He appoints, while we, in our personal dealings, are called to mercy and even love toward those who wrong us. God is the perfect Judge who will one day set every wrong right, which frees us to release our grievances to Him. Are you clinging to a right to retaliate that God is calling you to surrender to Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you clinging to a right to retaliate?
2. How does trusting God as Judge free you to show mercy?
3. Where is God calling you to overcome evil with good?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are the perfect Judge. Free me from the grip of revenge, and help me overcome evil with good. Amen.
